summary: Full backend + frontend test pass for AI Job Application Assistant. 32/32 pytest cases passed against Node/Express backend via FastAPI proxy. Frontend Playwright E2E covered login (valid + invalid), dashboard cards, Profile save + reload persistence, Job Analyzer (score 91% with strong matches, missing skills, education/experience cards, AI suggestions), Save Job, Track, Application CRUD, Resume upload, Extension page, and logout. No blocking issues found.

minor.issue: Non-PDF uploads reach controller and return 400 (correct), but very lax PDFs generated by reportlab/pdfkit/pdf-lib fail parsing with 422 due to bundled pdf-parse@1.1.1 using very old pdfjs-dist. Real-world PDFs (Word/Chrome export/pdf-parse fixture) parse fine. Consider upgrading to pdf-parse-fork or pdfjs-dist>=2.x for broader compatibility.

issues: Radix DialogContent missing aria-describedby (accessibility warning in console)

action_items: (Optional) Upgrade pdf-parse or use pdfjs-dist>=2.x so PDFs generated by modern libraries (reportlab, pdfkit, pdf-lib) also parse. Currently only PDFs already compatible with old pdfjs (Word/Chrome/most human resumes) work.
(Optional) Add DialogDescription or aria-describedby to Add-Application / other Radix dialogs.
critical_code_review_comments: authController uses bcryptjs (async hash + compare with 10 rounds) - OK. JWT_SECRET must be set in backend/.env (verified working).
profileController.updateProfile correctly does per-section merge, marks profile modified, and safely accepts partial updates.

jobMatchingService.computeMatch is fully transparent: only skills present in userSkills set (profile.professional.skills/programmingLanguages/frameworks/tools + resumeParsed.skills/technologies) count as strongMatches; missing skills go to `missing` list; never invents. Verified in test_match_never_invents_skills.

formMappingService correctly maps Full Name->fullName, Mobile Number->phone, University Name->university, LinkedIn Profile->linkedin; ambiguity between LinkedIn/Portfolio/GitHub handled via AMBIGUOUS_GROUPS.
FastAPI proxy (backend/server.py) is a thin reverse-proxy - fine. Uses httpx.AsyncClient with 60s timeout, strips hop-by-hop headers.
Frontend api.js correctly reads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and sends Bearer token from localStorage 'ja_token' on every request; 401 handler redirects to /login (except on /auth/me to avoid loop).
Resume upload multipart field name is `resume` (not `file`); this is fine but should be documented for extension developers.
seed_data_creation: Registered a few TEST_<uuid>@jobassist.com users during test runs; saved and deleted TEST jobs/applications/resumes as part of CRUD flow. Nothing lingering that would impact demo user's dashboard beyond a couple of TEST applications from UI Add-flow which can be pruned.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Real backend is Node/Express in /app/server. FastAPI proxy at /app/backend/server.py forwards 8001->5001. Resume upload multipart field = 'resume'. pdf-parse@1.1.1 only accepts PDFs compatible with old pdfjs-dist - use /app/server/node_modules/pdf-parse/test/data/01-valid.pdf as a known-good fixture for upload tests. All UI elements have solid data-testids. Auth: JWT Bearer via localStorage 'ja_token'. Chrome extension itself cannot be loaded in Playwright.
rca of the issue: No production-blocking bug found. The only friction encountered during automated testing was that PDFs generated by common Python libs (reportlab/fpdf2) or newer Node libs (pdf-lib, pdfkit) are not parseable by the pinned pdf-parse@1.1.1 (which uses a very old copy of pdfjs-dist). Mitigation: (a) upgrade to pdf-parse-fork or a modern pdfjs-dist wrapper, or (b) use the shipped test fixture PDF for automated tests, which we did.
